q-101832.name: Question 1
q-101832.worked_solution:
We need to isolate all terms with $f$ on one side of the equation. To do this, we start by subtracting $1$ from both sides: 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-3fg & =2f-1 \\ 1-3fg-1 & =2f-1-1 \\ -3fg & =2f-2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we subtract $2f$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3fg & =2f-2 \\ -3fg-2f & =2f-2-2f \\ -3fg-2f & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that all terms containing $f$ are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of $f$ are on the right-hand side.

Next, we factor out $f$ in the expression on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}-3fg-2f & =-2 \\ f(-3g-2) & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $(-3g-2)$ to isolate $f:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3g-2) & =-2 \\ \frac{f(-3g-2)}{-3g-2} & =\frac{-2}{-3g-2} \\ \frac{f\cancel{(-3g-2)}}{\cancel{-3g-2}} & =\frac{-2}{-(3g+2)} \\ f & =\frac{2}{3g+2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** This result assumes that $3g+2\ne 0.$

q-101832.html:
Question 1
?

If 1−3fg=2f−1, then f=

a
−32g−3
b
2g+13
c
−13g+2
d
23g+2
e
3g+22
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to isolate all terms with f on one side of the equation. To do this, we start by subtracting 1 from both sides:

1−3fg=2f−11−3fg−1=2f−1−1−3fg=2f−2

Next, we subtract 2f from both sides of the equation:

−3fg=2f−2−3fg−2f=2f−2−2f−3fg−2f=−2

Notice that all terms containing f are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of f are on the right-hand side.

Next, we factor out f in the expression on the left-hand side.

−3fg−2f=−2f(−3g−2)=−2

Finally, we divide both sides by (−3g−2) to isolate f:

f(−3g−2)=−2f(−3g−2)−3g−2=−2−3g−2f(−3g−2)−3g−2=−2−(3g+2)f=23g+2

Note: This result assumes that 3g+2≠0.

q-133848.name: Question 2
q-133848.worked_solution:
We need to isolate all terms with $g$ on one side of the equation. To do this, we start by subtracting $7$ from both sides: 

$$
\begin{aligned}11fg+7 & =f+4g \\ 11fg+7-7 & =f+4g-7 \\ 11fg & =f+4g-7\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we subtract $4g$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}11fg & =f+4g-7 \\ 11fg-4g & =f+4g-7-4g \\ 11fg-4g & =f-7\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that all terms containing $g$ are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of $g$ are on the right-hand side.

Then, we factor out $g$ in the expression on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}11fg-4g & =f-7 \\ g(11f-4) & =f-7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $(11f-4)$ to isolate $g:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(11f-4) & =f-7 \\ \frac{g(11f-4)}{11f-4} & =\frac{f-7}{11f-4} \\ \frac{g\cancel{(11f-4)}}{\cancel{11f-4}} & =\frac{f-7}{11f-4} \\ g & =\frac{f-7}{11f-4}\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** This result assumes that $11f-4\ne 0.$

Question 2
?

If 11fg+7=f+4g, then g=

a
f+117f−4
b
f+711f−4
c
f−117f−4
d
f−711f−4
e
7f11f−4
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need to isolate all terms with g on one side of the equation. To do this, we start by subtracting 7 from both sides:

11fg+7=f+4g11fg+7−7=f+4g−711fg=f+4g−7

Next, we subtract 4g from both sides of the equation:

11fg=f+4g−711fg−4g=f+4g−7−4g11fg−4g=f−7

Notice that all terms containing g are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of g are on the right-hand side.

Then, we factor out g in the expression on the left-hand side.

11fg−4g=f−7g(11f−4)=f−7

Finally, we divide both sides by (11f−4) to isolate g:

g(11f−4)=f−7g(11f−4)11f−4=f−711f−4g(11f−4)11f−4=f−711f−4g=f−711f−4

Note: This result assumes that 11f−4≠0.

q-215770.name: Question 3
q-215770.worked_solution:
We need to isolate all terms with $p$ on one side of the equation. To do this, we subtract $8p$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}5pq & =1+8p \\ 5pq-8p & =1+8p-8p \\ 5pq-8p & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that all terms containing $p$ are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of $p$ are on the right-hand side.

Next, we factor out $p$ in the expression on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}5pq-8p & =1 \\ (5q-8)p & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $(5q-8)$ to isolate $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(5q-8)p & =1 \\ \frac{(5q-8)p}{5q-8} & =\frac{1}{5q-8} \\ \frac{\cancel{(5q-8)}p}{\cancel{5q-8}} & =\frac{1}{5q-8} \\ p & =\frac{1}{5q-8}\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** This result assumes that $5q-8\ne 0.$

q-215794.name: Question 4
q-215794.worked_solution:
We need to isolate all terms with $q$ on one side of the equation. To do this, we first cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4pq+5}{5} & =\frac{4-3q}{3} \\ 3\cdot (4pq+5) & =5\cdot (4-3q) \\ 12pq+15 & =20-15q\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we add $15q$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}12pq+15 & =20-15q \\ 12pq+15+15q & =20-15q+15q \\ 12pq+15+15q & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we subtract $15$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}12pq+15+15q & =20 \\ 12pq+15+15q-15 & =20-15 \\ 12pq+15q & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that all terms containing $q$ are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of $q$ are on the right-hand side.

Then, we factor out $q$ from the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}12pq+15q & =5 \\ (12p+15)q & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $(12p+15)$ to isolate $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(12p+15)q & =5 \\ \frac{(12p+15)q}{12p+15} & =\frac{5}{12p+15} \\ \frac{\cancel{(12p+15)}q}{\cancel{12p+15}} & =\frac{5}{12p+15} \\ q & =\frac{5}{12p+15}\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** This result assumes that $12p+15\ne 0.$
